question: Which contact tracing method allows public health staff to reach out to partners privately without revealing the patient's name?

options.A: Direct self-testing
options.B: Client referral
options.C: Provider referral
options.D: Mandatory quarantine

explanation: That's provider referral! The health team steps in to handle the delicate notification confidentially, protecting the original patient's privacy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which type of medication is often prescribed to help manage chronic nerve pain?

options.A: Loop diuretics like furosemide
options.B: Inhaled short-acting beta-agonists
options.C: Broad-spectrum oral antibiotics
options.D: Anticonvulsants like gabapentin

explanation: Even though they were first made for seizures, anticonvulsants calm down wild, overactive nerve firing, making them great for shooting and burning nerve pain! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT something a community health nurse should do when promoting family planning?

options.A: Ensuring client confidentiality during health consultations
options.B: Dispelling common myths regarding modern contraceptive safety
options.C: Providing accurate counseling on various birth control options
options.D: Forcing community members to adopt specific contraceptive devices

explanation: You got it! Family planning must always be a personal choice. Forcing anyone goes against nursing ethics and human rights. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h6)

question: Why must hospital infection control guidelines be updated regularly?

options.A: To give hospital administrators something to do during slow months
options.B: To match the changing fashion trends of hospital uniforms
options.C: To adapt to shifting germ behaviors and new medical evidence
options.D: To ensure old paper manuals take up more space in the storage room

explanation: Correct! Germs change and grow stronger over time, so our safety rules must keep up with new science. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h4)

question: What is an easy, key nursing action to help prevent pneumonia in patients on a breathing machine (ventilator)?

options.A: Changing the endotracheal tube every twelve hours
options.B: Administering intravenous antibiotics to all ventilated patients
options.C: Keeping the room temperature below twenty degrees Celsius
options.D: Elevating the head of the bed between 30 and 45 degrees

explanation: Raising the bed head keeps oral and stomach secretions from sliding down into the lungs. Simple position changes make a massive difference! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which bacterium is most commonly responsible for causing osteomyelitis?

options.A: Escherichia coli
options.B: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Streptococcus pyogenes

explanation: Staph aureus is the heavy hitter behind most bone and joint infections. A great microbe to keep top of mind for your exams! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of a descriptive cross-sectional study?

options.A: To follow patients from birth until old age
options.B: To prove that one factor causes another over time
options.C: To show how common a health condition is in a population
options.D: To test the effectiveness of a new surgical tool

explanation: Descriptive studies simply lay out the facts—like how widespread a condition is—without trying to prove cause and effect. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is the most important infection control practice for nurses doing perineal care or dressing changes?

options.A: Using scented antiseptic soaps for all skin surfaces
options.B: Wearing sterile gowns for routine temperature checks
options.C: Isolating the mother from her newborn baby
options.D: Rigorous hand hygiene and aseptic technique

explanation: Simple hand hygiene and clean sterile technique are your absolute best defenses against bringing new germs into healing wounds. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h7)

question: Why do intersectoral teams sometimes struggle to communicate with each other?

options.A: Nurses refuse to share office space with workers from other government departments
options.B: Government policies legally forbid workers from different ministries from talking
options.C: Different professional sectors use unique terminology and focus on different priorities
options.D: Community leaders only communicate through written memos in foreign languages

explanation: Exactly! Every profession has its own special terms. If we don't use simple, shared language, misunderstandings happen easily. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h5)

question: During pin site care, why should you avoid scrubbing away dried crusts around the pins?

options.A: Crusts are needed to hold the metal pin tightly in place
options.B: Crusts act as a protective barrier against bacteria
options.C: Scrubbing crusts will cause the traction weights to fall off
options.D: Dried blood keeps the patient's scalp warm and dry

explanation: Hands off those crusts! They actually act like a natural little shield protecting the healing skin underneath from germs. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h6)

question: A 16-year-old patient is hesitant to talk about drug use while their mother sits right by the bed. What should you do?

options.A: Document that the patient is uncooperative and end the assessment
options.B: Force the patient to answer the questions in front of the parent
options.C: Threaten to call the police if the patient does not speak up
options.D: Ask the mother to step out briefly to ensure confidential communication

explanation: Spot on! Teens need a safe, confidential space to open up about sensitive topics without worrying about getting into trouble with their parents. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h5)

question: Why does showing great clinical skills make someone a better leader?

options.A: It allows them to work completely independently of doctors.
options.B: It prevents patients from ever filing formal complaints.
options.C: It exempts them from doing any paperwork during their shifts.
options.D: It sets a benchmark that encourages staff to strive for excellence.

explanation: Actions speak louder than words! When your team sees you performing nursing procedures with skill and care, they feel inspired to bring their A-game too. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why is it so important for you as a nurse to understand how a community functions?

options.A: To prescribe medications without needing a doctor
options.B: To manage hospital financial budgets and staff salaries
options.C: To understand how daily living conditions affect people's health
options.D: To diagnose rare genetic diseases in hospital laboratories

explanation: Spot on! The environment and everyday resources around your patients shape their health just as much as any medicine you give them. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T4#GNS225_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why do nurses care about catching cervical irritation early?

options.A: It prevents simple discomfort from progressing to chronic or ascending infections.
options.B: It immediately normalizes hormonal fluctuations during the menstrual cycle.
options.C: It guarantees that surgical intervention will never be required.
options.D: It completely eliminates the future risk of all pelvic inflammatory diseases.

explanation: Exactly! Catching inflammation early stops it from traveling up into the upper reproductive tract where it can cause bigger problems. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h1)

question: Why are professional nursing organizations important for your everyday life as a nurse?

options.A: They supply all consumable medical equipment to hospitals
options.B: They establish practice standards and shape health policies
options.C: They dictate the exact daily schedule of ward nurses
options.D: They manage direct disciplinary action for individual negligence

explanation: Think of these organizations as the voice of the profession. By creating guidelines and advocating for better policies, they help ensure safe, high-quality patient care everywhere. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the main use of calcium carbonate when taken as a mineral supplement?

options.A: Lowering high blood pressure through direct vasodilation
options.B: Neutralizing stomach acid and supporting bone strength
options.C: Stopping acute seizures in pregnant women with eclampsia
options.D: Thinning thick mucus secretions in the respiratory tract

explanation: Calcium carbonate doubles as a handy antacid for the tummy and provides essential calcium to build strong bones! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T3#GNS125_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which illegal substance is most commonly grown and used across Nigeria?

options.A: Ketamine
options.B: Cocaine
options.C: Heroin
options.D: Cannabis

explanation: Cannabis (often called weed or Igbo) is the most widely found illicit substance in Nigerian communities and clinics. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T11#GNS125_U2_T11_h3)

question: A nurse wants to understand the daily emotional experiences of mothers caring for children with chronic kidney disease. Which approach is best?

options.A: Qualitative phenomenology
options.B: Epidemiological survey
options.C: Quantitative correlational
options.D: Experimental clinical trial

explanation: Phenomenology sounds like a big word, but it just means studying the 'lived experience' of people going through a specific life event. Perfect for capturing their real stories! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is a common risk for a woman who uses a secret contraceptive method in a controlling relationship?

options.A: Mandatory enrollment in nursing leadership classes
options.B: Automatic promotion to a higher socioeconomic status
options.C: Instantaneous and permanent relief from all headaches
options.D: Experiencing partner violence or abandonment if found out

explanation: Using birth control without a partner's knowledge in environments with strict gender imbalances can provoke severe domestic conflict and safety risks. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h3)

question: Why does widespread use of antibiotics naturally lead to more resistant germs?

options.A: Drugs cause healthy human cells to mutate into resistant bacteria
options.B: Pathogens learn to consume the antibiotic drugs as a primary food source
options.C: Medicines expire quickly in tropical climates and lose their potency
options.D: Surviving microbes pass on their protective traits to the next generation

explanation: Think of it like survival of the fittest. When weak germs are killed off, the tough ones left behind breed and pass on their protective superpowers to their offspring! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h1)

question: Why is exact timing so important for blood draws during dynamic hormone tests?

options.A: Blood samples spoil if they sit at room temperature
options.B: Hormones disappear from the blood after five minutes
options.C: Laboratory technicians only work during morning hours
options.D: Hormone levels shift rapidly in response to specific triggers

explanation: Hormones react fast! Precise timing lets us catch the exact moment the gland reacts to our test medicine. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the main way azole antifungal drugs work?

options.A: Creating physical holes in the outer cell membrane
options.B: Preventing the conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol
options.C: Destroying the chitin layer of suppuration
options.D: Preventing the uptake of vital glucose molecules

explanation: Well done! Azoles block a key enzyme needed to make ergosterol. Without enough ergosterol, the fungal cell membrane weakens and fails. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h2)

question: What makes William Worden's grief theory different from the usual stage models?

options.A: It applies exclusively to elderly patients
options.B: It focuses only on the physical symptoms of dying
options.C: It states that grief ends completely within six weeks
options.D: It views grief as active tasks the person must work through

explanation: Great job! Instead of just passing through passive stages, Worden's model sees grief as a series of active steps or tasks the person works through to adapt. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T10#GNS321_U4_T10_h2)

question: During an acute asthma attack, why does a patient struggle to catch their breath?

options.A: Degeneration of skeletal muscle in the chest wall
options.B: Paralysis of the diaphragm skeletal muscle
options.C: Failure of cardiac muscle to pump blood to the lungs
options.D: Excessive contraction of airway smooth muscle

explanation: In asthma, the smooth muscle wrapped around the tiny airways spasms and squeezes shut, making it hard for air to move in and out. You'll see this often in practice! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h7)

question: What is a normal, expected feeling for a patient right after a sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: Mild belly bloating and the need to pass gas
options.B: Severe, sharp pain all over the stomach
options.C: Total numbness in both legs
options.D: An inability to pee for 24 hours

explanation: That's right! The air pumped into the bowel during the test has to come out somehow, causing temporary gas and bloating. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is a major benefit of primary nursing for patients?

options.A: Increased feelings of safety and better communication with a consistent nurse
options.B: Shorter waiting times in the hospital cafeteria
options.C: Elimination of all physical pain within twenty-four hours of admission
options.D: Guaranteed zero hospital bills upon discharge

explanation: Patients love seeing a familiar, caring face every day! It builds trust and cuts down the anxiety of hospital stays. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T3#GNS123_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the most important assessment for a nurse to make right after giving a rescue bronchodilator?

options.A: Capillary refill time in the fingers
options.B: Lung sounds and breathing effort
options.C: Deep tendon reflexes in the knees
options.D: Bowel sounds in all four quadrants

explanation: Since bronchodilators open up tight airways, listening to the patient's chest and watching their breathing effort is the quickest way to see if the treatment worked. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h4)

question: What is the very first thing you should do if a patient starts showing signs of an allergic rash after an injection?

options.A: Wait for thirty minutes to see if the rash disappears on its own
options.B: Ask the patient to write down her personal medical history
options.C: Stop the drug administration immediately and provide emergency care
options.D: Transfer the patient to a pharmacy for a replacement drug

explanation: Safety first! Always stop the medication right away to prevent any further reaction, then jump into emergency care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T11#GNS225_U3_T11_h8)

question: Why is environmental sustainability included as a core goal of food policy?

options.A: To reduce the total volume of crops grown worldwide
options.B: To prevent farmers from ever using modern machinery
options.C: To ensure that agricultural land is turned into housing estates
options.D: To protect soil and water resources for future food production

explanation: Sustainability ensures that farming practices do not ruin the environment, allowing continuous food production over the long term. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h2)

question: What is the main reason we give folic acid supplements in early pregnancy?

options.A: To stop maternal gestational hypertension
options.B: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: To prevent neural tube defects
options.D: To increase daily breast milk production

explanation: Folic acid is a tiny pill with a huge job! It protects the baby's developing brain and spine right from the very start. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h3)

question: Which test checks the speed and strength of electrical signals in a peripheral nerve?

options.A: Lumbar puncture
options.B: Nerve Conduction Studies
options.C: Electromyography
options.D: Magnetic Resonance Imaging

explanation: Nerve Conduction Studies use gentle, tiny electrical pulses on the skin to see how fast signals travel down the nerve highway. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h5)

question: Which professional group acts as the primary defense against prescribing and dosage errors before drugs reach the ward?

options.A: Medical records clerks
options.B: Ward porters
options.C: Pharmacists
options.D: Hospital accountants

explanation: Pharmacists review the initial orders and verify clinical safety before preparing the individual doses for distribution. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h5)

question: What actually is 'cor pulmonale'?

options.A: Bleeding into the chest cavity following trauma
options.B: An infection of the lining surrounding the lungs
options.C: Right-sided heart failure caused by long-term lung disease
options.D: A sudden collapse of a lung lobe due to a blocked airway

explanation: You nailed it. Long-term lung trouble makes the heart work extra hard on the right side, eventually leading to right-sided heart failure. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T12#GNS213_U2_T12_h3)

question: Which neonatal complication is commonly linked to fetal hyperinsulinemia delaying lung maturation?

options.A: Respiratory distress syndrome
options.B: Neonatal jaundice
options.C: Congenital heart murmurs
options.D: Necrotizing enterocolitis

explanation: High insulin levels can delay the production of lung surfactant, putting the newborn at a higher risk for respiratory distress syndrome. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h7)

question: Who on the subacute care team is usually responsible for assessing nutritional needs?

options.A: Occupational therapist
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Speech pathologist
options.D: Registered dietitian

explanation: Correct! Dietitians check nutritional status and plan the right meals or tube-feeding formulas to speed up healing. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h5)

question: Why do hospitals enforce strict double-key storage and witness counts for narcotics?

options.A: To prevent drug diversion and control abuse risks
options.B: To make medication administration take longer for nurses
options.C: To test whether the patient actually needs pain relief
options.D: To ensure the pharmaceutical company makes more profit

explanation: Strict counting and witness rules protect controlled substances from theft, misuse, or illegal diversion. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the minimum head-of-bed elevation for a patient on continuous tube feeding?

options.A: 30 to 45 degrees
options.B: 10 to 15 degrees
options.C: Flat on the back
options.D: 60 to 90 degrees

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the head of the bed raised prevents the formula from flowing backward into the lungs. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h6)

question: Which of these is part of the body's first line of defence?

options.A: Circulating blood antibodies
options.B: Intact skin and mucous membranes
options.C: Phagocytic white blood cells
options.D: Specialized T-lymphocyte cells

explanation: You got it! Your skin and mucous membranes act like a brick wall at the gate, stopping germs from entering your body in the first place. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T2#GNS123_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the main focus of community nutrition compared to hospital dietetics?

options.A: Promoting health for entire populations
options.B: Managing surgical recovery diets
options.C: Treating rare genetic disorders
options.D: Prescribing weight loss pills

explanation: Community nutrition looks at whole populations to prevent health problems, while hospital dietetics focuses on treating individual patients. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h1)

question: What is the body's main way of stopping hormone levels from climbing too high?

options.A: Enzymatic destruction
options.B: Receptor downregulation
options.C: Positive feedback
options.D: Negative feedback

explanation: Negative feedback is like a thermostat: when hormone levels get too high, a signal is sent to slow down production and bring things back to normal. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T3#GNS211_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is a major focus of modern family planning nursing?

options.A: Eliminating all forms of natural birth spacing methods
options.B: Providing equitable, community-based reproductive health education and care
options.C: Enforcing strict population limits on every family
options.D: Restricting contraceptive access exclusively to urban hospitals

explanation: Modern nursing is all about community outreach—making sure everyone can easily get reproductive health education and services. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h7)

question: Which of these is a common symptom of the genitourinary syndrome of menopause?

options.A: Excessive facial hair growth
options.B: Vaginal dryness and painful intercourse
options.C: Uncontrolled weight gain in the abdomen
options.D: Permanent loss of bladder sensation

explanation: Low estrogen makes the vaginal tissues thinner and drier, causing discomfort. Knowing this helps us care for patients with empathy. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T15#GNS121_U5_T15_h4)

question: Why do resource-limited regions often report higher rates of patient harm?

options.A: Local doctors have less formal education than foreign doctors
options.B: Medical technology in these regions is too advanced to operate
options.C: Weak infrastructure and understaffed facilities hinder safe care
options.D: Patients in these areas refuse to take their prescribed drugs

explanation: When hospitals lack steady power, enough staff, or basic supplies, it becomes much easier for errors to slip through. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T8#GNS312_U5_T8_h2)

question: Which medication is a classic historical drug used to treat severe cystinuria?

options.A: Furosemide
options.B: D-Penicillamine
options.C: Allopurinol
options.D: Spironolactone

explanation: D-Penicillamine was one of the very first thiol drugs used to bind cystine. While it works well, we have to watch out for its side effects! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T4#GNS223_U8_T4_h3)

question: What defines direct contact transmission?

options.A: Carrying of pathogens by biting insects like mosquitoes
options.B: Inhalation of tiny dried respiratory droplets floating in the air
options.C: Spread of germs through contaminated drinking water supplies
options.D: Physical transfer of pathogens between an infected person and a susceptible host

explanation: Direct contact requires physical touch or direct exposure to bodily fluids without any intermediary objects or surfaces. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the best way to start counselling a mother whose child is experiencing growth faltering?

options.A: Tell the mother to stop coming to the clinic until next year
options.B: Ask open-ended questions about recent feeding and illness
options.C: Scold the mother for failing to feed the child properly
options.D: Write a prescription for expensive imported vitamin supplements

explanation: Great nursing starts with empathy and listening. Ask gentle, open questions to understand what's happening at home without judging. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h8)

question: Why is it harmful when hospital departments operate in separate 'silos' without talking to each other?

options.A: It causes the hospital to run out of physical building space
options.B: It automatically increases the cost of medical equipment
options.C: It reduces the total number of patients admitted daily
options.D: It leads to severe delays and fragmented patient care

explanation: Great thinking! When units don't share info, patient care becomes scattered and delayed. Keeping the lines of communication open keeps our patients safe. [learn more](GST321_U1_T12#GST321_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why can a poor shift handover easily lead to a malpractice claim?

options.A: It automatically causes patients to fall out of their hospital beds
options.B: Crucial patient care details get lost, leading to missed treatments or delayed assessments
options.C: It forces doctors to perform nursing duties they are not trained for
options.D: It breaks hospital labor laws regarding nursing shift lengths

explanation: Good communication keeps patients safe! When handover is messy, important care steps get missed, which can harm the patient. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of the teach-back method in health education?

options.A: To evaluate the environmental noise levels in a clinic room
options.B: To document medical history in a formal hospital chart
options.C: To check if the client understands the instructions by having them repeat them
options.D: To test the nurse's ability to lecture a large community group

explanation: Teach-back allows nurses to verify comprehension by asking clients to explain back what was taught in their own words. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h8)

question: What is the most common symptom of acute oophoritis?

options.A: Complete stopping of sweating
options.B: Painless swelling of the abdomen
options.C: Severe pain in the upper right shoulder
options.D: Lower abdominal and pelvic pain

explanation: Because the ovaries are sitting in the pelvis, inflammation there directly causes lower tummy and pelvic pain that often hurts more when moving around. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T31#GNS216_U5_T31_h4)

question: Which symptom is the earliest and most reliable indicator of developing compartment syndrome?

options.A: Complete lack of any pulse felt in the foot or hand
options.B: Blue discoloration of the skin spreading rapidly over the toes
options.C: Severe, relentless pain that is not relieved by opioid pain medication
options.D: Total paralysis of all the fingers and toes on the affected limb

explanation: Intense, out-of-proportion pain that fails to respond to strong painkillers is the hallmark early warning sign of rising pressure inside a muscle compartment. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h6)

question: Why is visiting a patient's home so helpful for disease management?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any medications.
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never need a hospital visit.
options.C: It allows nurses to observe real-world habits and living conditions.
options.D: It places the entire workload on family members instead.

explanation: You get a true picture when you see where patients actually live! Home care lets you spot daily habits and environmental factors that directly affect their health. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T9#GNS324_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is the correct hand motion on the push rims when a patient is moving a manual wheelchair forward?

options.A: Grip at ten o'clock and push forward down to two o'clock
options.B: Grab the top of the wheels and pull backward continuously
options.C: Smack the spokes of the wheels with an open palm
options.D: Hold the hand rims tightly still while kicking the floor

explanation: Starting at ten o'clock gives the best mechanical advantage and long stroke length for efficient forward motion. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h5)

question: A patient taking ED meds is prescribed nitroglycerin for chest pain. What is your most critical nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to ignore the chest pain
options.B: Tell the patient to stop taking all physical exercise
options.C: Warn the patient about the fatal drop in blood pressure
options.D: Advise the patient to double their water intake daily

explanation: Crucial nursing catch! This is a textbook dangerous drug interaction that can cause severe, life-threatening hypotension. Always educate your patient! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T24#GNS312_U1_T24_h8)

question: Which of the following is checked during a social and practical support assessment?

options.A: Safety of the home environment and availability of caregivers
options.B: The exact microscopic cell count found in blood lab results
options.C: The specific brand of pain medication prescribed by the doctor
options.D: The patient's personal religious beliefs and church history

explanation: We check living conditions and who is around to help out, making sure the patient will be safe and supported at home. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is the main danger of disconnecting the catheter tubing from the drainage bag?

options.A: It breaks the closed system and lets bacteria enter
options.B: It triggers severe allergic reactions to the plastic
options.C: It causes immediate permanent damage to the urethral sphincter
options.D: It creates high pressure that bursts the balloon

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the drainage system sealed and closed is the single best way to protect your patient from getting a catheter-associated infection. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T20#GNS212_U1_T20_h7)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when turning an annoying ward problem into a research question?

options.A: Ordering expensive laboratory equipment for the ward
options.B: Reporting the nursing staff to the hospital board
options.C: Writing a textbook about the clinical problem
options.D: Focusing the observation onto clear, measurable variables

explanation: Start by breaking down your general frustration into specific pieces you can actually observe, count, or measure in the ward. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h5)

question: During which phase of healing do bone-building cells bridge a broken bone with spongy bone?

options.A: Fracture hematoma stage
options.B: Final remodeling stage
options.C: Bony callus formation
options.D: Initial inflammatory phase

explanation: In the bony callus phase, the body builds a temporary bridge of spongy bone across the break to stabilize it. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T20#GNS222_U1_T20_h5)

question: What is the main job of the circulating nurse during an operation?

options.A: Closing the surgical wound layers with sutures and staples
options.B: Managing the unsterile environment and monitoring patient safety
options.C: Performing the surgical incisions alongside the primary surgeon
options.D: Administering the general anesthetic gases to the patient

explanation: While the scrub nurse is sterile at the table, the circulating nurse moves freely around the room to coordinate supplies, record notes, and watch out for the patient's safety. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h3)

question: In Herzberg's theory, what is the main job of 'hygiene factors' like basic pay and a clean workplace?

options.A: Guarantees that every worker will achieve self-actualization
options.B: Determining which clinical nurses receive a promotion
options.C: Preventing job dissatisfaction rather than creating deep motivation
options.D: Replacing the need for monetary compensation in public hospitals

explanation: Hygiene factors stop people from complaining (like fixing a broken fan or paying salaries on time), but true job love comes from other things like feeling valued. [learn more](GST321_U1_T18#GST321_U1_T18_h3)

question: Which organ is the absolute MVP (main site) for drug metabolism in our body?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Kidneys

question: Why do nurses and therapists break big tasks like bathing into smaller, simple steps for neurological clients?

question: Which part of the Y-shaped antibody molecule binds directly to the antigen?

question: Clearing out stagnant water pools around houses is mainly done to control which element of disease spread?

question: Dizygotic (fraternal) twins are formed when:

question: Which component of cigarette smoke reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood?

question: Which of these are classified as micronutrients?

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of youth-friendly health services?

question: What does 'external validity' deal with?

question: Why is informed consent a crucial part of pre-test counselling?

question: Why is just counting calories often not enough when caring for a patient's nutrition?

question: Why is postpartum hemorrhage a huge risk after a mother delivers twins?

question: Why is treating an infected person usually not enough to stop a parasite outbreak on its own?

options.B: Parasites mutate into viral pathogens inside the human host
options.C: Laboratory tests cannot confirm when a patient is cured

question: Which form of a drug molecule passes most easily across biological cell membranes?

question: Which two techniques form the core of a routine musculoskeletal physical examination?

question: After a bronchodilator nebulizer treatment, a patient coughs heavily. What should the nurse encourage them to do next?

question: What does 'medication reconciliation' mean in home health care?

question: What is the final active form of vitamin D made by the kidneys?

question: What makes a Comprehensive EmONC center different from a Basic EmONC center?

question: What is the main financial goal of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR) programs?

question: When do Lassa fever outbreaks usually peak in Nigeria?

question: What is the term for the process where a tumor grows its own new blood supply?

question: Which group of viruses is most commonly spread through contaminated injection equipment?

question: Which vaccine is routinely given during antenatal care to protect the newborn against tetanus?

question: How do stimulant purgatives mainly get things moving in the gut?

question: Where do water-soluble hormones usually find their receptors?

question: How did Louis Pasteur's famous swan-neck flasks finally disprove spontaneous generation?

question: Which of these is a direct benefit of investing money into hospital technology?

question: What is a common social and physical complication of an untreated vaginal fistula?

question: Why is a basic knowledge of embryology important for nurses and midwives?

question: A patient starts crying while talking about a painful hospital memory during an interview. What should you do first?

question: How do Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs) mostly stop stomach acid?

question: Why is routine clamping of a chest tube strongly discouraged when moving a patient?

question: Where is the best place to keep emergency contact numbers in a patient's home?

question: Why must a prepared sterile field never be left unattended by the nurse?

question: What are vital statistics primarily records of?

question: How can a nurse show cultural humility when facing traditional family hierarchies?

question: Why is comprehensive sexuality education more effective than just telling teens to practice abstinence?

question: A stroke patient is trying to stick out their tongue, but it keeps pulling to one side. Which muscle is likely affected?

question: What is the main goal of home health care?

question: How do abdominal thrusts (the Heimlich maneuver) help a choking person?

question: Why do nurses do a baseline neurological check when a patient first arrives?
